llm.summary: The skill's code, instructions, and persistence behavior are coherent with its stated purpose (a local ZTO helper); it stores data under ~/.openclaw/data/zto and uses a local encrypted store but does not request unrelated credentials or reach out to unexpected endpoints.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (ZTO shipment helper) matches the included files and functionality: tracking simulation, estimates, history, subscriptions, and local address storage. No unrelated credentials, binaries, or system access are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md describes workflows and explicitly documents local persistence paths and privacy operations. The runtime code follows these instructions and confines reads/writes to ~/.openclaw/data/zto and its secure subdirectory. There are no instructions to read unrelated system files or exfiltrate data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is instruction-plus-code (no platform install spec). requirements.txt lists common Python packages (aiohttp, cryptography, etc.) appropriate for a local CLI. No arbitrary external download URLs or archive extraction are used.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or external credentials. Local storage of user data and an on-disk encryption key are used for convenience and are documented in SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill writes only to its own data paths under ~/.openclaw/data/zto (and ~/.openclaw/data/zto/secure). always is false and the skill does not attempt to modify other skills or system-wide agent settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be what it says: a local ZTO helper that persists history, subscriptions, and optional saved addresses under ~/.openclaw/data/zto and stores an encrypted key in ~/.openclaw/data/zto/secure/.key (file mode 600). If you install/run the code: (1) be aware it will create the database and encrypted storage under those paths; (2) installing the Python deps (requirements.txt) will pull packages like cryptography and aiohttp via pip — only install from trusted sources; (3) use the provided privacy commands (privacy info / privacy clear / privacy export) if you want to inspect or remove local data; and (4) review the code if you require absolute assurance (the encryption key is stored locally so disk access to that path would allow decryption).
